paragraphs.text: More than 25 years ago, Saroo Brierley lived in rural (农村) India. One day, he played with his brother along the rail line and fell asleep. When he woke up and found himself alone, the 4-year-old decided his brother might be on the train he saw in front of him - so he got on.

That train took him a thousand miles across the country to a totally strange city. He lived on the streets, and then in an orphanage (孤儿院) . There, he was adopted by an Australian family and flown to Tasmania.

As he writes in his new book, A Long Way Home, Brierley couldn’t help but wonder about his hometown back in India. He remembered landmarks, but since he didn’t know his town’s name, finding a small neighborhood in a vast country proved to be impossible.

Then he found a digital mapping program. He spent years searching for his hometown in the program’s satellite pictures. In 2011, he came across something familiar. He studied it and realized he was looking at a town’s central business district from a bird’s-eye view. He thought, “on the right-hand side you should see the three-platform train station” -and there it was. “And on the left-hand side you should see a big fountain”- and there it was.
Everything just started to match.

When he stood in front of the house where he grew up as a child, he saw a lady standing in the entrance. “There’s something about me,” he thought -and it took him a few seconds but he finally remembered what she used to look like.

In an interview Brierley says, “My mother looked so much shorter than I remembered. But she came forth and walked forward, and I walked forward, and my feelings and tears and the chemical in my brain, you know, it was like a nuclear fusion (核聚变) . I just didn’t know what to say, because I never thought seeing my mother would ever come true. And here I am, standing in front of her.”

At the start of the 20th century, an American engineer named John Elfreth Watkins made predictions about life today. His predictions about slowing population growth, mobile phones and increasing height were close to the mark. But he was wrong in one prediction: that everybody would walk 10 miles a day.

Today, in Australia, most children on average fall 2,000 steps short of the physical activity they need to avoid being overweight. In the early 1970s, 40 per cent of children walked to school, while in 2010, it was as low as 15 per cent.

The decline is not because we have all become lazy. Families are pressed for time, many with both parents working to pay for their house, often working hours not of their choosing, living in car-dependent neighborhoods with limited public transport.

The other side of the coin is equally a deprivation: for health and well-being, as well as lost opportunities (机会) for children to get to know their local surroundings. And for parents there are lost opportunities to walk and talk with their young scholar about their day.

Most parents will have eagerly asked their child about their day, only to meet with a “good”, quickly followed by “I’m hungry”. This is also my experience as a mother. But somewhere over the daily walk more about my son’s day comes out. I hear him making sense of friendship and its limits. This is the unexpected and rare parental opportunity to hear more.

Many primary schools support walking school-bus routes (路线) , with days of regular, parent-accompanied walks. Doing just one of these a few times a week is better than nothing. It can be tough to begin and takes a little planning - running shoes by the front door, lunches made the night before, umbrellas on rainy days and hats on hot ones-but it’s certainly worth trying.

Researchers say they have translated the meaning of gestures that wild chimpanzees (黑猩猩) use to communicate. They say wild chimps communicate 19 specific messages to one another with a “vocabulary” of 66 gestures. The scientists discovered this by following and filming groups of chimps in Uganda, and examining more than 5,000 incidents of these meaningful exchanges.

Dr. Catherine Hobaiter, who led the research, said that this was the only form of intentional communication to be recorded in the animal kingdom. Only humans and chimps, she said, had a system of communication where they deliberately sent a message to another group member.
“That’s what’s so amazing about chimp gestures,” she said. “They’re the only thing that looks like human language in that respect.”

Although previous research has shown that apes and monkeys can understand complex information from another animal’s call, the animals do not appear to use their voices intentionally to communicate messages. This was a significant difference between calls and gestures, Dr. Hobaiter said.

Chimps will check to see if they have the attention of the animal with which they wish to communicate. In one case, a mother presents her foot to her crying baby, signaling: “Climb on me.” The youngster immediately jumps on to its mother’s back and they travel off together. “The big message from this study is that there is another species (物种) out there that is meaningful in its communication, so that’s not unique to humans,” said Dr. Hobaiter.

Dr. Susanne Shultz, an evolutionary biologist from the University of Manchester, said the study was praiseworthy in seeking to enrich our knowledge of the evolution of human language. But, she added, the results were “a little disappointing”.

“The vagueness of the gesture meanings suggests either that the chimps have little to communicate, or we are still missing a lot of the information contained in their gestures and actions,” she said. “Moreover, the meanings seem to not go beyond what other animals convey with non-verbal communication. So, it seems the gulf remains.”

paragraphs.text: You run into the grocery store to pick up one bottle of water. You get what you need. head to the front, and choose the line that looks fastest.
You chose wrong. People who you swear got in other lines long after you are already checked out and off to the parking lot. __31__ 1
It turns out, it’s just math working against you; chances are, the other line really is faster.

Grocery stores try to have enough employees at checkout to get all their customers through with minimum delay. __32__ 2   Any small interruption – a price check, a chatty customer – can have downstream effects, holding up an entire line.

If there are three lines in the store, delays will happen randomly at different registers. Think about the probability: __33__ 3   So it’s not just in your mind: Another line probably is moving faster.

Researchers have a good way to deal with this problem. Make all customers stand in one long, snaking line – called a serpentine line – and serve each person at the front with the next available register. __34__ 4   This is what they do at most banks and fast-food restaurants. With a serpentine line, a long delay at one register won’t unfairly punish the people who lined up behind it. Instead, it will slow down everyone a little bit but speed up checkout overall.
__35__ 5   It takes many registers to keep one line moving quickly, and some stores can’t afford the space or manpower. So wherever your next wait may be: Good luck.

BMI is an internationally recognized measurement tool __57__gives an indication of whether someone is a healthy weight. It is calculated by dividing a __58__ (person) weight in kg by their height in meters squared, and a BMI of between 19 and 25 __59__ (consider) healthy.

The study found that between 1985 and 2017, average rural BMI increased__60__2.1 in women and men. In cities, however, the gain __61__ (be) 1.3 in women and 1.6 in men. 假定你是李华，下周有新西兰学生访问你校，你将作为学生代表致欢迎辞。请为此写一篇发言稿，内容包括：
1. 表示欢迎； 2. 介绍活动安排；3. 表达祝愿。
1. 词数80左右；
2. 可适当增加细节，以使行文连贯。

Pumpkin (南瓜) carving at Halloween is a family tradition. We visit a local farm every October. In the pumpkin field, I compete with my three brothers and sister to seek out the biggest pumpkin. My dad has a rule that we have to carry our pumpkins back home, and as the eldest child I have an advantage -I carried an 85-pounder back last year.

This year, it was hard to tell whether my prize or the one chosen by my 14-year-old brother, Jason, was the winner. Unfortunately, we forgot to weigh them before taking out their insides, but I was determined to prove my point. All of us were hard at work at the kitchen table, with my mom filming the annual event. I’m unsure now why I thought forcing my head inside the pumpkin would settle the matter, but it seemed to make perfect sense at the time.

With the pumpkin resting on the table, hole uppermost, I bent over and pressed my head against the opening. At first I got jammed just above my eyes and then, as I went on with my task, unwilling to quit, my nose briefly prevented entry. Finally I managed to put my whole head into it, like a cork (软木塞) forced into a bottle. I was able to straighten up with the huge pumpkin resting on my shoulders.

My excitement was short-lived. The pumpkin was heavy. “I’m going to set it down, now,” I said, and with Jason helping to support its weight, I bent back over the table to give it somewhere to rest. It was only when I tried to remove my head that I realized getting out was going to be less straightforward than getting in. When I pulled hard, my nose got in the way. I got into a panic as I pressed firmly against the table and moved my head around trying to find the right angle, but it was no use. “I can’t get it out!” I shouted, my voice sounding unnaturally loud in the enclosed space.

group-zj-2021-jan-reading-a.overview: 本文是一篇人物记叙文，讲述印度男孩 Saroo Brierley 四岁时与家人意外失散、被澳大利亚家庭收养，二十多年后借助数字地图卫星图像找到家乡、最终与母亲重逢的真实故事。

discourseStructure.summary: 按时间顺序展开：先交代失散起因，再写被收养与远赴塔斯马尼亚，接着写他寻找家乡的困难与最终借助数字地图程序定位成功，最后落到与母亲重逢的情感高潮。

paragraphs.summary: 二十多年前，住在印度农村的四岁男孩 Saroo 在铁路边玩耍睡着，醒来发现独自一人，以为哥哥在眼前的火车上便上了车。
paragraphs.function: 交代故事背景与失散的起因。

paragraphs.summary: 火车把他带到千里之外一座陌生城市，他流落街头后进入孤儿院，在那里被一个澳大利亚家庭收养并飞往塔斯马尼亚。
paragraphs.function: 叙述失散后的经历与被收养的转折。

paragraphs.summary: 他在新书《A Long Way Home》中写到自己始终牵挂印度的家乡，虽记得一些地标，但因不知家乡名字，在广袤国土上寻找一个小社区几乎不可能。
paragraphs.function: 引出他寻根的愿望与面临的巨大困难。

paragraphs.summary: 他找到一款数字地图程序，多年在卫星图中搜索，2011 年发现熟悉的中央商务区鸟瞰图，并按记忆验证出三站台火车站和大喷泉。
paragraphs.function: 叙述借助数字地图找到家乡的关键过程。

paragraphs.summary: 一切开始逐一对上号。
paragraphs.function: 承上启下，强调记忆与画面完全吻合，推动情节走向重逢。

paragraphs.summary: 当他站在儿时长大的房子前，看到门口站着一位女士，过了几秒终于回忆起她当年的样子。
paragraphs.function: 铺垫与母亲相认的瞬间。

paragraphs.summary: 在采访中他描述与母亲重逢的强烈情感：母亲走上前，他走上前，泪水与脑中化学反应如同核聚变，他从未想过见到母亲会成真。
paragraphs.function: 以采访中的自述呈现与母亲重逢的情感高潮。

group-zj-2021-jan-reading-b.overview: 本文是一篇议论性说明文，探讨现代儿童步行量（尤其是步行上学）减少的现象、原因及其代价，并由作者以母亲身份现身说法，指出与孩子一起步行的额外价值，最后倡导参加“步行校车”路线。

discourseStructure.summary: 文章从一个百年前的预言切入引出话题，先用数据说明步行减少的现状，再分析原因（家庭时间紧张而非懒惰），接着论述步行减少在健康与亲子交流上的双重损失，作者用自身经历佐证步行带来的亲子沟通机会，结尾发出参加步行上学路线的倡议。

paragraphs.summary: 20世纪初工程师Watkins对今日生活做出多项预言，多数命中，唯独“人人每天步行10英里”落空。
paragraphs.function: 以历史预言作引子，引出当今步行量减少这一话题。

paragraphs.summary: 用澳大利亚的数据说明儿童运动量不足，步行上学比例从1970年代初的40%降到2010年的15%。
paragraphs.function: 用具体数据呈现儿童步行减少的现状，提出问题。

paragraphs.summary: 指出步行减少并非因为人们变懒，而是家庭时间紧张、父母双职工、居住在依赖汽车、公共交通有限的社区。
paragraphs.function: 分析步行减少的真正原因，排除“懒惰”这一误解。

paragraphs.summary: 步行减少的另一面同样是损失：损害健康，孩子失去认识周边环境的机会，父母失去与孩子边走边聊的机会。
paragraphs.function: 论述步行减少在健康与亲子交流上的双重代价。

paragraphs.summary: 作者以母亲身份现身说法：平时问孩子只换来“good”和“我饿了”，但在每天的步行途中却能听到更多，了解孩子如何理解友谊及其界限，这是难得的亲子沟通机会。
paragraphs.function: 用作者自身经历佐证步行带来的、了解孩子内心的宝贵机会。

paragraphs.summary: 许多小学支持有家长陪同的“步行校车”路线，每周做几次胜过完全不做；起步虽难、需要规划，但值得尝试。
paragraphs.function: 提出可行倡议，呼吁参加步行上学路线，收束全文。

group-zj-2021-jan-reading-c.overview: 本文是一篇科普说明文，报道研究者破译野生黑猩猩用手势进行交流的研究成果，并引入正反两方面专家观点：主导研究的 Hobaiter 博士强调黑猩猩与人类一样能有意图地传递信息，进化生物学家 Shultz 博士则认为研究虽有价值但结果有限，人猿之间的鸿沟依然存在。

discourseStructure.summary: 全文先抛出研究发现（手势词汇与含义），再由主导研究者阐释其与人类语言的相似之处与意义，最后引入另一位专家的批评，形成正反对照的讨论结构。

paragraphs.summary: 研究者称已破译野生黑猩猩用手势交流的含义：用 66 种手势传递 19 条特定信息，基于在乌干达拍摄的 5000 多次交流实例。
paragraphs.function: 引出研究主题与核心发现

paragraphs.summary: 主导研究的 Hobaiter 博士指出这是动物界唯一被记录到的有意图交流，只有人类和黑猩猩会刻意向同伴发送信息。
paragraphs.function: 提出研究的核心论点：有意图的交流

paragraphs.summary: Hobaiter 引述黑猩猩手势之惊人，称其是唯一在此方面类似人类语言的东西。
paragraphs.function: 强化论点，突出与人类语言的相似性

paragraphs.summary: 尽管以往研究显示猿猴能理解同类叫声中的复杂信息，但它们并非有意图地用声音传递信息，这是叫声与手势的重要区别。
paragraphs.function: 对比叫声与手势，凸显手势的有意图性

paragraphs.summary: 黑猩猩会先确认对方注意力，如母猩猩伸脚示意幼崽爬上背；Hobaiter 总结人类并非唯一会进行有意义交流的物种。
paragraphs.function: 举例佐证并总结研究意义

paragraphs.summary: 进化生物学家 Shultz 博士认为该研究在丰富人类语言进化知识方面值得称赞，但结果有点令人失望。
paragraphs.function: 引入第二位专家的正反评价，转折

paragraphs.summary: Shultz 指出手势含义模糊，或说明黑猩猩没什么可交流，或说明我们仍漏掉大量信息；其含义未超出其他动物的非语言交流，人猿鸿沟依旧。
paragraphs.function: 展开批评，给出全文的保留性结论

optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 是一次失败，但方法值得称赞。

trap.sourceQuote: the study was praiseworthy in seeking to enrich our knowledge of the evolution of human language. But, she added, the results were “a little disappointing”.
trap.optionText: It was a failure but the methods deserved praise.
trap.explanation: 原文称研究本身 praiseworthy、结果只是 a little disappointing（有点失望），程度温和；选项却把整项研究定性为 failure（失败），并把称赞错位到方法上，态度颠倒且与原文不符。

trapEvidence.anchor: 研究值得称赞，而非失败

locationParaphrases.sourceText: It was a good try but the findings were limited.
locationParaphrases.targetText: the study was praiseworthy in seeking to enrich our knowledge of the evolution of human language. But, she added, the results were “a little disappointing”.
locationParaphrases.note: 选项 a good try 对应 praiseworthy in seeking to...（值得称赞的尝试），the findings were limited 对应 results were a little disappointing 以及第七段含义未超出其他动物的说明。

q-zj-2021-jan-029.questionFocus: 考查末段 gulf 的词义，需借助上下文（人猩交流的差异讨论）推断其指人与动物之间的差距。
q-zj-2021-jan-029.stemTranslationZh: 末段中划线词 “gulf” 是什么意思？

evidence.quote: the meanings seem to not go beyond what other animals convey with non-verbal communication. So, it seems the gulf remains.
evidence.anchor: 含义未超出其他动物，故差距依旧

evidence.quote: this was the only form of intentional communication to be recorded in the animal kingdom
evidence.anchor: 人猩交流与其他动物的差距背景

trap.explanation: 末段讨论的是人类语言与动物非语言交流之间的“差距”，并无任何对立或争斗之意，“冲突”与语境不符，属无中生有。

trap.sourceQuote: the meanings seem to not go beyond what other animals convey with non-verbal communication. So, it seems the gulf remains.
trap.explanation: 上文 not go beyond 与 the gulf remains 表明人猩交流与其他动物间仍存在落差、并未拉平；“平衡”意味着两者相当，与原文强调的差距方向相反。

trap.sourceQuote: the meanings seem to not go beyond what other animals convey with non-verbal communication. So, it seems the gulf remains.
trap.explanation: gulf 表示鸿沟、差距，remains 表示其依然存在，强调人与动物交流之间的“隔阂”；“联系/关联”意思相反，方向颠倒。

locationParaphrases.targetText: the meanings seem to not go beyond what other animals convey with non-verbal communication
locationParaphrases.note: 由 not go beyond what other animals convey（未超出其他动物的交流）这一上文线索可推知 gulf 指人与动物交流间的 difference（差距）。

q-zj-2021-jan-030.questionFocus: 考查全文最佳标题，需把握主旨：研究破译了黑猩猩用于交流的手势含义，同时保留人猩仍有差距的结论。
q-zj-2021-jan-030.stemTranslationZh: 下列哪项是本文最佳标题？

optionAnalysis.label: A
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 黑猩猩行为研究取得突破。

trap.optionText: Chimpanzee behaviour study achieved a breakthrough
trap.explanation: 全文主题是“手势交流”的破译，而非泛泛的“行为研究”，且第六、七段明确指出结果令人失望、鸿沟仍在，谈不上 breakthrough（突破），选项范围与程度均拔高。

trapEvidence.anchor: 结果令人失望，并非突破

optionAnalysis.label: B
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 黑猩猩发展出特定的交流技能。

trap.sourceQuote: Researchers say they have translated the meaning of gestures that wild chimpanzees (黑猩猩) use to communicate.
trap.explanation: 文章重点是研究者“破译/翻译”了黑猩猩既有手势的含义，而非黑猩猩“发展出”交流技能；developed 把研究发现偷换成黑猩猩自身能力的演化，偏离主旨。

trapEvidence.quote: they have translated the meaning of gestures that wild chimpanzees
trapEvidence.anchor: 研究破译手势含义，非黑猩猩发展技能

optionAnalysis.label: C
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 黑猩猩：动物界最聪明的物种。

trap.claim: Chimpanzees: the smartest species in the animal kingdom
trap.explanation: 全文聚焦黑猩猩手势交流与人类语言的对比，从未将黑猩猩与其他动物比较并断言其“最聪明”，the smartest species 在文中没有依据，属无中生有。

optionAnalysis.label: D
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 黑猩猩语言：交流手势被破译。

evidence.quote: Researchers say they have translated the meaning of gestures that wild chimpanzees (黑猩猩) use to communicate.
evidence.anchor: 研究者破译黑猩猩用于交流的手势含义

evidence.quote: They’re the only thing that looks like human language in that respect.
evidence.anchor: 手势在此方面类似人类语言

locationParaphrases.targetText: they have translated the meaning of gestures that wild chimpanzees (黑猩猩) use to communicate
locationParaphrases.note: 标题 communication gestures translated 直接对应首段 translated the meaning of gestures ... use to communicate，language 则呼应第三段 looks like human language，准确概括全文主旨。
